title: Duke Ellington's hotel trouble in London
summary: Albertson recalls the 1931-era report that Ellington was refused a room until it was known he was not West Indian.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Now, I remember reading in the Chicago Defender from -- I believe it was 1931 -- very early '30's anyway -- there was a long article about some problems Duke Ellington was having and had had in London, getting a hotel room, and I recall when they found out that he wasn't West Indian, everything was okay.
But when they thought he was West Indian, then --
Because, you know, during the war they told the West Indians -- the West Indians wanted to go back and help. They said, no, don't come. Stay where you are. They didn't want them.
